title: Understanding and evaluating computer vision models through the lens of counterfactuals

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluated using Attribute-Specific Adversarial Counterfactuals (ASACs) to measure and mitigate bias in image classifiers (via DEO, DEOp, and DDP metrics), and via LLM-generated counterfactual prompts to measure distributional shifts in text-to-image generative models using VQA-based Concept Association Scores (CAS) and Mean Absolute Deviation (MAD).

Measured in classifiers using adversarial counterfactuals, and in text-to-image models by altering age descriptors in prompts and quantifying intersectional dependencies using VQA attribute extraction and Wasserstein distance-based Intersectional Sensitivity scores.

Evaluated in generative models by comparing images generated from baseline prompts versus prompts with substituted racial or ethnic terms, analyzing the outputs through VQA-extracted visual concepts and computing CAS and MAD.

Assessed by dynamically generating counterfactual prompts introducing disability-related concepts (e.g., 'wheelchair', 'hearing aid', 'blind') and measuring the resulting visual differences using VQA concept matching and similarity metrics.
Measured by altering cultural background modifiers in text-to-image prompts and evaluating the shifts in depicted visual concepts and aesthetics using VQA-based Top-K concept extraction.
Evaluated dynamically by prompting large language models to identify relevant socioeconomic counterfactuals for an input prompt and analyzing the generated image sets using targeted VQA questions.

Measured by modifying physical descriptors (e.g., 'obese', 'slim', 'muscular') in generation prompts and analyzing the intersectional impacts on other traits (like gender or clothing) using causal graphs and Intersectional Sensitivity.
Evaluated by generating counterfactual prompts involving different religious contexts and comparing the visual semantics of the generated images using VQA and Concept Association Scores.
